rulings.challenge_claim: The row's stated ground for clustering 24:5-6 -- "the strength/power vocabulary carrying across both verses" -- is not byte-true: v6 contains no strength/power term at all.
rulings.grounds: Byte tier (oshb:Prov.24.5 "גֶּֽבֶר חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ כֹּֽחַ"; oshb:Prov.24.6 "כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה וּ֝תְשׁוּעָ֗ה בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ"), re-derived independently. v5 carries two strength/power tokens, בַּע֑וֹז (oz, "in strength") and כֹּֽחַ (koach, "power"), plus the strengthening verb מְאַמֶּץ; v6 contains neither token nor any strength synonym -- confirmed by direct byte read, zero strength/power lexemes present. The row's stated warrant fails verification as written. A correct, byte-available warrant exists and was left unnamed: v6 opens with כִּ֣י (byte-confirmed at token 0), the identical declarative-plus-ki-motive construction the sibling admonition_unit rows in this span open their own motive verses with -- re-verified here at 24:12 (כִּֽי), 24:16 (כִּ֤י), and 24:20 (כִּ֤י), all three token-0 byte matches.
rulings.remedy: In P10-024's rationale, delete the byte-false clause "the strength/power vocabulary carrying across both verses"; install the ki-motive warrant instead -- v6's opening particle explains how v5's strength is exercised (strategy/counsel in war), matching the same construction already cited as cohesion evidence at 24:11-12, 24:15-16, 24:19-20. Test the cure must pass: any strength/power token cited as "carrying across" must independently sweep-hit v6 (it currently does not -- the test that killed the original); the substituted ki-motive claim must show v6's first token is the ki-particle at the byte tier (already confirmed). One composite edit covers this and the OL item below.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that no building-vocabulary token repeats past verse 4 overlooks an undisclosed wisdom-term recurrence at the row's own seam (da'at at 24:4 and 24:5).
rulings.grounds: Skeleton tier. וּ֭בְדַעַת (24:4) and דַּ֝֗עַת (24:5) do share the root d-'-t, confirmed at skeleton tier (not byte-identical strings, since the 24:4 form carries a vav+bet prefix) -- OL's narrow textual claim is correct, and the row's device_notes overclaim ("the two figures share no token at their seam") is byte-false as a general statement, even though the row's rejected_alternative is narrowly scoped to "building-vocabulary" token and that narrower claim survives (house/rooms do not recur past v4). However, the challenge's implicit severity is overstated: sweep.py --skel on this root returns 44/915 verses book-wide (re-verified, matching LF's own count on P10-023), and unlike the rare catchwords this same packet treats as genuine (zimmah 13/915 sole-adjacent at 24:8-9; kashal 6/915 sole-adjacent at 24:16-17), this root recurs adjacently FIVE separate times book-wide (2:5-6, 8:9-10, 14:6-7, 22:19-20, plus 24:4-5 -- a new finding beyond either packet's own disclosure), so its 24:4-5 adjacency is not distinguishing. This matches LF's own dismissal of the identical link on P10-023 ("too common a wisdom-vocabulary term to carry independent cross-seam weight"). Refine: the byte-fact is real and the device_notes overclaim needs correcting, but this is common-vocabulary texture, not an independent boundary-relevant catchword -- same composite defect as the LF item, not a second, separate defect.
rulings.remedy: Same field/edit as the LF item above (one composite remedy, not two): correct P10-024's device_notes from "kept separate since the two figures share no token at their seam" to an accurate, scoped statement -- no building-vocabulary token repeats past v4; the common wisdom-root recurs at 24:4|24:5 but is textural (44/915 book-wide, 5 adjacent-pairs elsewhere), not an independent catchword. Test the cure must pass: the corrected device_notes claim must survive a full token-level (not just building-vocabulary-subset) diff between v4 and v5.

rulings.challenge_claim: The claim that 24:17 "opens a fresh prohibition unrelated to the wicked-man-ambush warning just closed" is contradicted by a rare, byte-verified shared root (kashal) linking 24:16-24:17, and the row's rejected_alternative only tests the weaker forward rival, never engaging the stronger backward link.
rulings.grounds: Byte + skeleton tier (oshb:Prov.24.16 "כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע יִפּ֣וֹל צַדִּ֣יק וָקָ֑ם וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ בְרָעָֽה"; oshb:Prov.24.17 "בִּנְפֹ֣ל אויביך אֽ֭וֹיִבְךָ אַל תִּשְׂמָ֑ח וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ אַל יָגֵ֥ל לִבֶּֽךָ"). v16 closes יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ, v17 continues וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ -- root k-sh-l, re-verified via sweep.py --skel = 6/915 (4:12, 4:19, 16:18, 24:16, 24:17, 26:1), and 24:16-24:17 is confirmed the sole adjacent pair in that list -- matching this packet's own bar for a genuine, non-coincidental catchword (identical structure to the zimmah precedent at 24:8-9). The row's rejected_alternative tests only merging FORWARD with 24:19-20 ("a fresh doubled imperative reopens at 24:19"); it never engages the backward rival that 24:17-18 could continue 24:15-16's wicked-man scene. The row's "unrelated" framing is unsupported as stated.
rulings.remedy: One composite remedy covers this and the OL item below (see that entry).

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's characterization of 24:17 as opening a prohibition unrelated to the ambush warning just closed overlooks an undisclosed root recurrence from 24:16 (nafal).
rulings.grounds: Byte tier. v16 יִפּ֣וֹל (Qal imperfect, assimilated nun, compensatory dagesh) and v17 בִּנְפֹ֣ל (infinitive construct, unassimilated nun) are the same root n-p-l -- confirmed by direct pointed-byte inspection; sweep.py --skel on the unassimilated string alone returns only 2/915 (24:17, 30:18) because the skeleton-substring search cannot catch v16's assimilated form, so this is a root/lexical-tier finding, not a skeleton-sweep hit (re-verified; matches LF's own tier note on the same fact). Together with LF's independent kashal finding (item above), this is the SAME underlying defect converging from two directions: the row's "unrelated" framing at 24:17 is contradicted by TWO separate byte-true root echoes at the 24:16|17 seam, and its rejected_alternative never tests the backward rival either root points to. Ruled as ONE composite defect with the LF item, not two.
rulings.remedy: Composite remedy for P10-031 (both LF and OL items, one edit): in the rationale, remove or qualify "opens a fresh prohibition unrelated to the wicked-man-ambush warning just closed"; disclose both root-echoes (kashal -- rare, sole-adjacent; nafal -- same root, assimilated/unassimilated) at the 24:16|17 seam. Expand rejected_alternative to test the backward rival (continuity with 24:15-16) alongside the existing forward rival (24:19-20), naming a positive reason the unit still opens fresh despite the echoes (e.g., an address-shift from third-person wicked-man narration to second-person reader address), or concede the tension if no such reason holds. Test the cure must pass: the revised rejected_alternative must explicitly name and answer BOTH rivals, not only the forward one (the test that exposed the original gap). Boundary/granularity change (e.g., merging 24:15-18) is NOT authorized by this remedy -- it is a proposal only, for explicit boss adoption, per the brief's scope limit on peer rulings.
